title: Planaria resist cancer and ageing despite noisy genomes via pattern completion

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Planaria resist cancer and ageing despite noisy genomes via pattern completion

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In silico simulations show how lineages such as planarian flatworms can become extremely resistant to transgenesis, ageing, cancer and injury despite very noisy genomes because they commit to a strategy that overrides genetic details with large-scale pattern completion.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2024, Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue › 4. Beyond the Brain: Bowties Everywhere

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: In silico simulation results [176] show how this kind of process can give rise to remarkable lineages, such as planarian flatworms, which are extremely resistant to transgenesis, aging, cancer, and injury despite40 their incredibly noisy genome because they have fully committed to a strategy that overrides genetic details with large-scale pattern completion [176].

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue”, Entropy (Basel, Switzerland) (2024), doi:10.3390/e26060481; section “4. Beyond the Brain: Bowties Everywhere”. Scope: Planarian flatworms (e.g. Schmidtea mediterranea) and in silico evolutionary models

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-memory-11: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.53

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The in silico component has a clear intervention and can in principle be reimplemented, while the mapping to planarian biology is much less discriminating. Existing public resources could resolve the model result but not the full historical inference.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Reproduce the cited evolutionary simulation and compare lineage robustness under increasing genome noise with and without a large-scale pattern-completion controller. Robustness specifically emerging in the pattern-completion condition supports the simulation claim; equal failure or robustness under controls refutes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Several empirical resistance traits are bundled together.

Code availability for the cited model is uncertain.

Simulation support does not establish that real planaria use the same mechanism.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public assemblies can test the noisy-genome half, and the regeneration literature is large, so that portion of the statement is partly checkable. Tumor resistance and lack of aging are not settled by a public longitudinal dataset, and the causal appeal to an in silico pattern-completion strategy cannot be rerun from a deposited model. Genomic data alone do not discriminate that mechanism from other explanations of planarian robustness.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Quantify planarian genome heterozygosity, repeat content, and ploidy variation from public assemblies, and set those beside published rates of regeneration, tumor formation, and actuarial aging. The pattern-completion cause would further require re-running the cited evolutionary simulation and showing that disabling pattern completion removes the resistance.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Cancer resistance and negligible senescence are not quantified in one cohort dataset.

The pattern-completion simulation is not a clearly reusable public code base.

A noisy genome co-occurring with regeneration does not show that pattern completion is the cause.
